title: Identity and access (IAM): users, roles and policies

videos.script: Anything that touches a cloud account makes a request. A person at a console, a script on a laptop, a function running at three in the morning. The provider asks each of them the same question. Who is this, and may they do this, to this thing, right now? {{question}} Get the answer wrong in one direction and nothing works. People notice that at once and complain. Get it wrong in the other direction and nobody complains at all. A key pasted into a repository works for whoever finds it. A role that could do far more than its job needed does all of it for the person who borrows it. {{wrong}} This lesson gives you the vocabulary every provider shares. Users and groups for people. Roles for programs and for visitors. Policies that say what each of them may do. {{parts}} You will read a policy line by line. Then you will learn the rule that decides every request: nothing is allowed until something allows it, and one deny beats every allow. {{rule}} After that, you will see how a program on a server gets credentials without anybody typing a password. And you will see the same ideas under their names at Google Cloud and Azure. {{names}} There is no cloud account in this course. The only commands here are ones a laptop answers with no credentials at all. {{laptop}}
